model: Aurora UPC, Variable Speed Water-Source Heat Pump
applies_to: WaterFurnace variable speed water-to-air heat pumps with Aurora controls and the Aurora UPC.
summary: BACnet objects of the Aurora UPC on a variable speed water-source heat pump, software version 1.03. Besides occupancy, setpoints and alarms it exposes compressor drive data (speed 0-12, inverter and drive temperatures, line and DC bus voltage), EEV position, variable speed pump settings, hot water (DHW), humidification and demand controlled ventilation points.
notes: Object names are the sheet's reference names. BV 98-102 have no reference name in the source, so their display names are used.
Many points are marked 'do not map' in the source and are listed only for completeness.

The dip switch and alarm pages at the back of this sheet are copied from the dual-compressor list: they cite dual-compressor addresses (BV 24-39, BV 44/45, AV 80/81, MSV 6/7) that are missing here or mean something else. Use this list's own points (BV 11-22, AV 44, MSV 8). MSV 8 states are taken from that alarm table's MSV column; confirm codes on site.
The source shows BV 88 e_stop_st states as Normal/Load Shed.
Transport and network settings come from the Aurora UPC Application and Troubleshooting Guide (AG1568EW), which is written for the single-compressor UPC.

source.title: Aurora UPC BACnet Points List For Variable Speed WSHP

integration.summary: Keep BV 54 at External and command occupancy on MSV 1; AV 145 sets the unit mode (off, auto, heat, cool, emergency heat). The UPC holds the occupied, unoccupied and standby setpoints (AV 5-10). Read MSV 11 for the operating mode and MSV 8 for the lockout code; AV 147 shows the compressor speed step.

minimum_points.name: schedule_select_cmd
minimum_points.why: Must be External for BAS occupancy commands

minimum_points.name: op_mode
minimum_points.why: Mode command: 0 off, 1 auto, 2 heat, 3 cool, 4 em heat

minimum_points.name: alarm_reset_cmd
minimum_points.why: Reset manual-reset alarms (On, then back to Off)

integration.enable: BV 54 schedule_select_cmd picks the internal schedule or external BAS commands (External is the listed default). Occupancy commands go to MSV 1, or to AV 42 after BV 50 is set to AV. AV 145 op_mode sets off/auto/heat/cool/emergency heat. BV 25 e_stop_cmd shuts the unit down.
integration.remote_sensors: AV 4 zone_temp_ovrd replaces the zone sensor once BV 55 zone_temp_selector is set to BAS. AV 17 humidity_cmd, AV 22 co2_cmd and AV 24 voc_cmd accept BAS values when no sensor is connected, and AV 26 oat_cmd takes an outdoor air temperature.
setup: Port 1a is the BAS port: EIA-485 for BACnet MS/TP (or N2), set by DIP switches, with baud 9600, 19.2k, 38.4k or 76.8k. It ships set to BACnet at 38,400 baud. (From AG1568EW, written for the single-compressor UPC.)
Port 1a can instead be jumpered for ARC156 (BACnet over ARCNET at 156 kbps). A LonWorks plug-in card uses port 1b and disables port 1a.
The MAC address is set on two rotary switches (tens and ones), 1 from the factory and 99 at most. The UPC only reads a new address after a power cycle.
The device instance is built from the network number and the MAC: network 7000 with MAC 12 gives 7012.
Wiring: 22 or 24 AWG shielded twisted pair, daisy-chained, polarity-sensitive (Net+, Net-, shield). About 30 devices and 2,000 ft per trunk; every MAC on a trunk must be unique.
gotchas: Unlike the single and dual compressor UPC lists, this one has no network G/Y1/Y2 command points; control is by occupancy, mode and setpoints.
Dip switch overrides (BV 11-18) only pass to the ABC while BV 22 is enabled; record the physical switch settings first.
BV 86 archive_now stores configuration changes; the sheet says archives should be limited.
Alarm reset: command BV 5 On, then back to Off.
